tex_content.html:
Proposition
1. ch2:2.7

↗ def:local-isometry ↗ def:metric-preserving ↗ def:isometry ↗ lem:metric-preserving-equidim-local-diffeomorphism For equal-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, a smooth map is a local isometry if and only if it preserves the metric.
Proof

↗ def:local-isometry ↗ lem:metric-preserving-equidim-local-diffeomorphism \sketch A local isometry preserves the metric on each neighborhood, hence everywhere. Conversely, metric preservation and Lemma 3 give local diffeomorphisms; their restrictions preserve the metric and are local isometries.

□

A Riemannian $n$-manifold is flat when every point has a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of Euclidean $n$-space. Isometries of $(M,g)$ form the group $\operatorname {Iso}(M,g)$ under composition.
